messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered: P1 - inference-pipeline high tail latency in us-west (page: pagerduty.com/INC12345) :rotating_light:
alex: I'm on it. seeing a spike in queue depth across the realtime queue (q.realtime.v2).
maria: Confirmed, dashboards show queue depth from ~120 -> 240 in 3m, 99p latency > 5s. Customer error rate creeping up.
ryan: GPU pool gpool-usw2-2 at 98% alloc, lots of load_model events. Warmup tasks are queued.
sophie: Any autoscaler events? HPA or our custom scaler logs?
alex: HPA events show no scale-up in the same window. cpu/util stayed ~45% per pod but queue_throttle metric high. Looks like pod CPU isn't the signal we want for this workload.
maria: sharing quick logs: `kubectl logs -n infra autoscaler-68f9 | tail -n 80` -> "no scale: cpu below threshold" + backlog_hint ignored.
ryan: grep from runtime logs: `grep "start_warmup" -n /var/log/runtime/* | tail -n 50` -> many warmup tasks show 30-45s delay between request and start_warmup. model load times spiking.
sophie: So hypothesis A: HPA CPU threshold prevented scale-up; B: model load/warmup backlog making pods effectively unavailable even if CPU signal low.
alex: mitigation I did: forced scale to 60 replicas for q.realtime.v2 (kubectl scale --replicas=60 deployment/realtime-v2) and enabled warmup_pool for 4 extra gpus (infra API call). Latency dropped after ~40s.
maria: customer impact: A subset of streaming customers saw delayed responses and 502s for ~4m. Support notified.
ryan: attaching timeline snippet I built: 2415012300 alert rule fires (latency), 2415012330 queue depth climb, 2415012342 first pager, 2415012350 autoscaler log shows "no-op", 2415012360 forced scale by alex, 2415012405 latency recedes.
sophie: adding forensic commands I used: `curl -s http://metrics/api/query?m=queue.depth` and `aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --metric-name GPUUtil` for correlation.
infra-bot: Note: warmup-pool toggle ON for gpool-usw2-2 by alex at 2415012360.
alex: For in-incident RCA: steps to collect - (1) full autoscaler logs (2) pod-level model-load traces (3) HPA config + recent edits (4) traffic routing rules. I'll paste the autoscaler dump in #incidents-logs.
maria: Quick ask to next oncall: please verify HPA policy and consider switching to queue-backlog-based scaler or lower CPU threshold for realtime route.
ryan: I captured `journalctl` slices showing OOM? No OOMs, just long pulls from model registry (registry latency spiked). Registry latency correlate: 2415012325-2415012380 -> 500ms+ pulls.
sophie: Hypothesis ranking in-thread: 1) autoscaler signal mismatch (high) 2) registry/model pull latency causing warmup backlog (medium) 3) GPU pool fragmentation/packing (medium) 4) transient routing burst (low).
alex: Agree. Action items: A) infra to investigate registry latency (ryan), B) infra to evaluate warmup pool sizing and prefetch (alex+ryan), C) runtime team to add queue-based scaler ticket (sophie), D) support to send customer impact note (maria).
maria: I'll draft the customer note and send to support-review within 30m.
ryan: I'll take registry metrics and open a short postmortem section with logs.
sophie: I'll create a tracker card and tag teams. Leaving a short handoff now — oncall until 2415016000. Please escalate if perf recurs.
alex: Handoff: root cause provisional = autoscaler signal mismatch + registry-induced warmup backlog. Next steps documented in /docs/incidents/INC12345-draft.md.
incident-bot: Incident INC12345 acknowledged and marked: in-progress -> mitigated. :white_check_mark:
